title: Integral inverse image preserves $\Dbc$ and agrees with the completed inverse image
statement:
Let $g\colon X\to Y$ be a morphism of standing schemes and
$g^*\colon\D(Y_{\mathrm{proét}},\mathcal O_E)\to\D(X_{\mathrm{proét}},\mathcal O_E)$ the inverse image.

1. $g^*$ maps $\Dbc(Y,\mathcal O_E)$ into $\Dbc(X,\mathcal O_E)$.
2. For $K\in\Dbc(Y,\mathcal O_E)$ the natural map
   $$
   c_K\colon g^*K\longrightarrow R\varprojlim_ng^{-1}\bigl(K\otimes^{\mathbf L}\mathcal O_E/\pi_E^n\bigr)
   $$
   is an isomorphism. After restriction of scalars to the constant sheaf
   $\underline{\mathcal O_E}$ the target is the completed inverse image of
   the Stacks Project (Stacks, Tags 099I, 099N), so on
   $\Dbc(-,\mathcal O_E)$ the inverse image $g^*$ agrees with the completed inverse
   image.

proof.text: Put $R_T=\mathcal O_{E,T}$, $C_T=(\mathcal O_E)_T$ (the discrete constant sheaf), and $A_{n,T}=(\mathcal O_E/\pi_E^n)_T$. The cartesian coefficient statement gives $g^{-1}R_Y\cong R_X$ and $g^{-1}A_{n,Y}\cong A_{n,X}$, and identifies module pullback with the exact functor $g^{-1}$. Thus it is computed termwise on complexes, preserves distinguished triangles (it commutes with shifts and the finite direct sums and differentials defining mapping cones), and $H^q(g^*N)=g^*H^q(N)$: apply the exact functor to kernels and images of the differential. In particular it preserves a given cohomological bound. The module pullback composition isomorphisms will identify restrictions after base change.

source.place: first paragraph; exactness and coefficient identifications

proof.text: Here is the elementary finite-presentation argument needed for the local models. For a constructible $R_T$-module $F$ on a standing scheme $T$ and a morphism $h:T'\to T$, choose its finite stratification and, on each stratum $S$, a pro-étale covering $W_j\to S$ with presentations $R_{W_j}^{r_j}\xrightarrow{B_j}R_{W_j}^{s_j}\to F|_{W_j}\to0$, where $B_j$ has entries in $\mathcal O_E$. The base-changed strata form a finite stratification of $T'$. The inverse-image construction sends the covering to its base-changed covering. On $W_j\times_TT'$ exact pullback and the cartesian coefficients give the same presentation with the same scalar matrix $B_j$ over $R_{W_j\times_TT'}$. This is a finite constant local model, so $h^*F$ is constructible by its definition. Empty strata are simply discarded.

source.place: Local models: base-changed covering and unchanged scalar matrices

proof.text: For an open immersion $j:U\hookrightarrow T$ of standing schemes, write $i:Z\hookrightarrow T$ for its closed complement, and let $j':U'\hookrightarrow T'$ and $i':Z'\hookrightarrow T'$ be their base changes by $h:T'\to T$. The schemes are Noetherian, so these opens are quasi-compact as morphisms. Take $N\in D^b(U,R_U)$; this is the case needed for the generators below. Adjunction gives $\beta:j'_!h_U^*N\to h^*j_!N$: its adjoint is $h_U^*N\cong j'^*h^*j_!N$, using pullback composition and $j^*j_!\cong\mathrm{id}$. The adjunction triangle identity makes $j'^*\beta$ the identity under these identifications; $i'^*\beta$ is $0\to0$ by $i^*j_!=0$ and pullback composition. Exactness preserves cohomological bounds, so $C=\operatorname{Cone}(\beta)$ is bounded and the cited $D^+$ localization triangle applies. Its two end terms $j'_!j'^*C$ and $i'_*i'^*C$ are zero, hence $C=0$. Thus $h^*j_!N\cong j'_!h_U^*N$ for these bounded complexes.

source.place: Tags 09AA (lemma-closed-immersion), 09BN (lemma-open-immersion), 09AH (lemma-ses-associated-to-open); adjunction calculation of open base change

proof.text: For the closed immersion in the square of step 3, take $N\in D^b(Z,R_Z)$. The unit for $i'^*\dashv i'_*$ gives $\gamma:h^*i_*N\to i'_*i'^*h^*i_*N\cong i'_*h_Z^*N$. The last identification uses pullback composition and $i^*i_*\cong\mathrm{id}$. The adjunction triangle identity makes $i'^*\gamma$ the identity under these identifications, and $j'^*\gamma$ is $0\to0$ since $j^*i_*=0$. Both $i_*$ and $i'_*$ are exact because their complementary opens are quasi-compact, so $C=\operatorname{Cone}(\gamma)$ is bounded. In its localization triangle $j'_!j'^*C\to C\to i'_*i'^*C\to$, the two end terms vanish, hence $C=0$ and $h^*i_*N\cong i'_*h_Z^*N$. For a locally closed immersion factor $a=i\circ u:S\hookrightarrow\overline S\hookrightarrow T$, with $u$ open and $i$ closed. For bounded $M$ the two calculations give $h^*i_*u_!M\cong i'_*h_{\overline S}^*u_!M\cong i'_*u'_!h_S^*M=a'_!h_S^*M$. All complexes entering these calculations remain bounded by exactness.

source.place: Tags 09AA (lemma-closed-immersion), 09BM (lemma-closed-immersion-complement-retrocompact-exact), 09AH (lemma-ses-associated-to-open); adjunction calculation of closed base change

proof.text: Consider a generator $a_!M$ supplied by clause (2) of [det-lem-int-tensor-shriek]. Write $S'=S\times_YX$ and $g_S:S'\to S$. On the base-changed local-model covering, $g_S^*M$ is the same bounded finite free scalar complex $P_j\otimes_{\mathcal O_E}R_{W'_j}$, by termwise exact pullback and coefficient compatibility. To check membership without assuming any commutation of arbitrary inverse image with inverse limits, use $M\in\Dbc(S,\mathcal O_E)$: its finitely many nonzero cohomology sheaves are constructible, and the finite-presentation argument of step 2 shows that their pullbacks are constructible. Step 1 gives the same bounds and identifies these with the cohomology of $g_S^*M$. Thus $g_S^*M\in\Dbc(S',\mathcal O_E)$. Clause (1) of [det-lem-int-tensor-shriek] gives $a'_!g_S^*M\in\Dbc(X,\mathcal O_E)$, and steps 3--4 identify this with $g^*a_!M$.

source.place: Local models; preservation on stratum generators

proof.text: The full subcategory of $\Dbc(Y,\mathcal O_E)$ consisting of $N$ for which $g^*N\in\Dbc(X,\mathcal O_E)$ is closed under isomorphisms and the two-out-of-three operation on distinguished triangles: by clause (1) of [sk-lem-int-integral-heart] applied on both schemes, two vertices in $\Dbc(Y,\mathcal O_E)$ force the third to lie there; $g^*$ takes that triangle to a triangle, and the triangulatedness of $\Dbc(X,\mathcal O_E)$ gives the same conclusion for their pullbacks. It contains every generator of step 5. Clause (2) of [det-lem-int-tensor-shriek] therefore implies that it contains every $K\in\Dbc(Y,\mathcal O_E)$. This proves (1), by the finite-stratum dévissage required by the unit.

Apply the criterion in clause (2) of [sk-lem-integral-models] to the object $g^*K$ just proved bounded constructible. The scheme $X$ is in its separated finite-type characteristic-$p$ setting, and $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ is finite with $\ell\ne p$, exactly as required. The same criterion applies to $K$ on $Y$. In particular both $K$ and $g^*K$ are derived $\pi_E$-complete. Consequently its canonical unit $g^*K\to R\varprojlim_n(g^*K\otimes^L_{R_X}A_{n,X})$ is an isomorphism, by [sk-def-pe-derived-completion]. Only the criterion in clause (2) is used here, not the preservation assertion in clause (3).

source.place: Local models and comparison paragraphs: integral criterion, now applied after dévissage

proof.text: Derived tensor compatibility for ringed-topos pullback gives natural isomorphisms $g^*(K\otimes^L_{R_Y}A_{n,Y})\cong g^*K\otimes^L_{R_X}A_{n,X}$. Naturality in the second variable makes these commute with $A_{n+1}\to A_n$ and with the quotient maps out of $K$. Use the functorial strict reduction-tower construction of [def-weil-pbc-completed-pullback], not an unspecified cone of unrelated maps. It therefore identifies the displayed unit in step 7 with precisely $c_K$ in the statement, including its transition maps and its map from $g^*K$. Since $g^*=g^{-1}$ on these coefficient modules, its target is the stated $R\varprojlim_ng^{-1}(K\otimes^L A_{n,Y})$. Thus $c_K$ is an isomorphism.

source.place: first paragraph: compatible reduction tower and completion unit

proof.text: Finally $R_T\cong\varprojlim_n A_{n,T}$ by [det-prop-sfb-qlbar-colimit-x-integral-limit]. The cartesian coefficient isomorphism in [sk-prop-sfb-cartesian-coefficients] identifies the source $\operatorname{Res}_X(g^*K)$ canonically with $g^{-1}\operatorname{Res}_Y K$: the scalar-extension map is an isomorphism because $g^{-1}R_Y\to R_X$ is one. Restriction of scalars $C_T\to R_T$ has, by [lem-weil-pbc-constant-completion-equivalence], the natural finite-reduction comparison, its compatibility with pullback and quotient transitions, and preservation of the derived limits of these strict towers and their completion units. Hence the restriction of the target of $c_K$ is $R\varprojlim_ng^{-1}(\operatorname{Res}_Y K\otimes^L_{C_Y}A_{n,Y})$, with the same comparison map. By [sk-lem-integral-models] (1),(2), $\operatorname{Res}_Y K$ is an object of the constant-coefficient derived-complete constructible category. The last paragraph of [def-weil-pbc-completed-pullback] identifies exactly this tower and its unit with the Stacks completed inverse image (Tag 099N, proetale-lemma-pushforward-Noetherian-case, clauses (2),(5)). This proves the scalar-restriction assertion in (2).

Expanded immersion base change from recollement, proved constructible local-model pullback by scalar presentations, and deduced completeness from the existing criterion after dévissage. Identified the canonical strict-tower unit and its scalar restriction. Reused existing nodes throughout; no new nodes.
split_report.blueprint: First paragraph -> steps 1,8; Local models -> steps 2--5,7; Dévissage -> step 6; Comparison with the Stacks Project -> step 9. Completeness is checked after constructibility using the existing criterion, avoiding unsupported product-preservation assertions.

tool_uses.why: Exact inverse image and identification of integral and finite coefficient sheaves; a coefficient-system tool, not a replacement for dévissage.
Base change of the finite constructible stratification; geometric bookkeeping for the unchanged local-model route.
Open/closed adjunctions and localization triangle detect the explicitly constructed base-change maps; no six-functor finiteness assertion is imported.
Exactness, vanishing cross-restrictions, and restriction identities for the same open/closed calculation.
Only the constant/completed comparison and derived-completeness criterion (1),(2), never its pullback-preservation clause (3).
Generic monoidality and naturality of derived module pullback identify the finite reduction tower.
Identification of the completed integral coefficient ring with the limit of finite constant coefficients.
Generic coefficient-restriction comparisons including strict derived limits and units; the unit has no more specific tower-coherence lemma.
